sent_to_model:
I need help writing a public review of the hike I did with my girlfriend on the Echo Canyon side. I'm from Colorado, so I figured the warnings about the difficulty were probably overdoing it. That didn't last very long once we got going. I had a really good time, even with a few scrapes coming back down. I want to give it four stars and give other hikers a useful idea of the climbing, the view, and why the parking and trail markings cost it a star. I'd like to include our experience and a little practical advice for people going.

- Had to leave the car at Barry Goldwater Memorial, some distance from the hike.
- I'm from Colorado; visited with my girlfriend.
- Went around 4pm; relatively few people at the summit.
- Used the Echo Canyon route; hadn't known another trail existed.
- Nearby streets didn't allow parking; parking at the hike wasn't available to us.
- Summit panorama extended a long distance all around.
- Several small route mistakes; each was fairly quick to correct.
- Minor cuts and scraped knees happened during the descent.
- Some hikers run the route in both directions.
- The route included stairs and a steep section with a handrail.
- Other hikers apparently also sustained minor injuries.
- Read difficulty warnings before going; neither of us initially took them very seriously.
- Scrapes came from catching rocks while stepping over them without raising my legs enough.
- Occasionally climbed toward a dead end and had to find the actual route.
- My girlfriend considered the stairs insufficiently challenging for hiking; the steep handrail climb changed her assessment.
- Choosing routes over the rocky sections made the climb especially enjoyable.
- Enormous homes visible immediately below were astonishingly extravagant.
- Among my favorite hiking and climbing experiences anywhere.
- Experience itself deserves five stars; parking and insufficient route markers reduce my rating to four.
- People running this terrain seem reckless to me.
- Visitors should expect genuinely demanding terrain despite the initial stairs.
- Recommend deliberate foot placement and a patient pace to avoid minor injuries.

(About me: recreational hiker. Length: it should come to roughly 250-400 words.)

must_cover: The hike proved challenging despite the writer's initial confidence.
The climbing was enjoyable and the summit offered expansive views.
Parking difficulties and inadequate trail markings lowered the rating to four stars.
The descent caused minor scrapes, with careful movement recommended.

reference.kind: a real piece of writing by a real person
